before: Before a take, choose how you read the scene and how you’ll play it. Each brief supports two readings or more, and none is the right answer: a reading changes what the take is judged on most and which abilities it calls on, shifting the balance and adding nothing, and the beat whose tones lean its way most counts more, where one beat does. How you’ll play it comes as three choices, each between two ways or left open: Pace (Measured or Driven), Scale (Restrained or Expansive) and Structure (Set or Open). Choosing a way isn’t rehearsing it: you rehearse it on your feet before it pays off.
after: Before you tape a brief, choose how you read the scene and how you’ll play it, in the brief under Your Reading and How You’ll Play It. Each brief supports two readings or more, and none is the right answer: a reading changes what the take is judged on most and which abilities it calls on, shifting the balance and adding nothing, and the beat whose tones lean its way most counts more, where one beat does. How you’ll play it comes as three choices, each between two ways or left open: Pace (Measured or Driven), Scale (Restrained or Expansive) and Structure (Set or Open). Choosing a way isn’t rehearsing it: you rehearse it on your feet before it pays off.
why: “Before a take” left a new player not knowing what a take is or where the choices are.
